findings.issue_text: Duplicate definition of `downsize` in app/models/optimized_image.rb: the new 4-param version silently overrides the existing 5-param one, breaking existing callers with ArgumentError
downsize loop in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-69 writes ImageMagick output to the same path it reads from, which ImageMagick refuses or corrupts
Passing "80%" as the dimensions argument to downsize_instructions/downsize_instructions_animated produces malformed geometry/command lines for animated GIFs, causing server-side upload failures

Hardcoded 10 * 1024 limit in utilities.js:182 and :246 decouples client-side gate from max_image_size_kb server setting, making the downsizing feature unreachable for files between the setting and 10MB
Client-side check drops max_attachment_size_kb, hardcoding a 10MB ceiling for all upload types, blocking larger attachments the admin configured
413 handler hardcodes 'max 10MB' in the alert regardless of the server's actual limit or nginx client_max_body_size, giving wrong rejection reasons
No handling for when 5 downsize attempts still leave an image over max_image_size_kb, resulting in a raw 'file too large' rejection
Downsize failure is silently ignored; in-place from == to downsize corrupts the tempfile when ImageMagick fails or is killed mid-write, uploading corrupted bytes
def self.downsize is defined twice in the same class body, shadowing the first definition and breaking existing two-argument callers with invalid ImageMagick geometry
Animated GIFs are silently converted to static images when allow_animated_thumbnails is off; allow_animated_avatars is never consulted and original upload animation is destroyed
No tests or assertions for any of the changed behavior, including the convergence loop, in-place file mutation, method redefinition, and client-side limit change
Client-side size check in utilities.js:182 hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types, silently disabling admin-configured limits like max_attachment_size_kb for non-image uploads
Hardcoded 10MB client-side message desynchronizes from actual server-side enforced limit, showing users '10MB' when server rejects at a different setting value
413 handler in utilities.js:246 always claims a 10MB limit even when the server rejected at a type-specific setting, misleading users about attachments
uploads_controller.rb:55 hardcodes the API-URL download cap at 10MB via FileHelper.download, discarding SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb for the API path

Downsizing loop in uploads_controller.rb:63-70 enforces no invariant that the file ends up under the limit; after 5 failed attempts or when convert_with returns false, the oversized tempfile is passed to Upload.create_for with no size check or user-facing error

Unscoped refactor of OptimizedImage's resize/downsize/optimize signatures from (width, height) to a free-form dimensions string, weakening type safety for existing callers and deleting dimensions(width, height)

Ruby method redefinition: downsize is defined twice in optimized_image.rb; the second definition silently shadows the first, so old 5-argument callers pass opts into dimensions and produce garbage geometry strings

Downsizing only fires when FileHelper.is_image?(filename), and filename from URI.parse(url).path may lack an extension for API-downloaded files, so downsizing silently never runs for extension-less API uploads

uploads_controller.rb:63-68 uses the same tempfile.path as both from and to in OptimizedImage.downsize, corrupting the upload file because ImageMagick truncates the output before fully reading the input
uploads_controller.rb:64-68 passes '80%' as the dimensions argument, which is not valid for the rewritten optimize pipeline expecting 'WxH' format parsed via split("x")
uploads_controller.rb:62-69 downsize loop has no success check or failure path, so still-oversized files proceed to Upload.create_for if 5 iterations of 80% scaling can't reach max_image_size_kb

utilities.js:182 and :246 hardcodes a 10MB client limit while the server still enforces the configurable SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, producing guaranteed user-facing failures and misleading 413 error messages
optimized_image.rb:145-147 defines a duplicate downsize method; the first definition is dead code and any 4-arg call gets silently reinterpreted by the second definition
uploads_controller.rb:68 performs blocking 5x full-image convert forks on the request path, risking web worker saturation for concurrent large uploads
Client-side size gate hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring admin-configured max_image_size_kb and per-type settings, so files between the configured limit and 10MB pass client validation
Files between configured limit and 10MB get silently downsized server-side or fail at Upload.create_for with an error contradicting the pre-upload message
413 error path reports a fixed 10MB limit instead of the actual max_image_size_kb enforced by the server, misleading users to retry under a limit that will fail again
Downsizing loop mutates the user's uploaded file in place before validation, changing contract from rejecting oversized images to silently altering them without consent or notice
Downsizing potentially strips animation via allow_animation: allow_animated_thumbnails, a thumbnail-specific setting, and applies to every image above the limit even if it would otherwise be rejected

downsize overload collapses width/height into a free-form dimensions string; passing '80%' uses ImageMagick percentage geometry which upscales and does not respect the shrink-only size-bounds contract existing callers rely on
Server-side download size limit replaced with hardcoded 10.megabytes, discarding SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, allowing bypass of admin-configured bandwidth/disk controls

DoS amplification via repeated synchronous shell-outs: OptimizedImage.downsize runs up to 5 times per upload on attacker-supplied bytes with no timeout or shrink check, enabling decompression-bomb CPU exhaustion
Content-type/size validation gate trusts client-controlled filename extension (FileHelper.is_image?) instead of content-sniffing magic bytes, allowing non-image payloads to pass and compound DoS
Client-side size ceiling hardcoded to 10 * 1024 KB, removing SiteSetting['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] enforcement from UX and causing misleading user-facing errors

app/models/optimized_image.rb:142-148 — `def self.downsize` is defined twice in the same module; the second definition silently overrides the first, so callers using the 4-arg form pass `max_width` as the `dimensions` string and drop `max_height`, producing incorrectly-sized thumbnails or failed convert calls

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-70 — the downsize loop mutates `tempfile` in place but `Upload.create_for` reads `tempfile.size` after the loop; if ImageMagick fails (exitstatus swallowed by `convert_with`), the oversized file is passed to `Upload.create_for` causing errors
app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-70 — the filename's original extension / extension-vs-content is never re-validated after downsizing

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-70 — the loop uses "80%" geometry, which under the new string-dimensions signature is a percentage scale rather than a pixel bound, so 5 passes yield at most ~67% linear reduction, failing silently for large images with no user feedback

OptimizedImage.downsize overwrites the source tempfile in place with a lossy resample, permanently destroying the user's original upload even if the upload ultimately fails validation, with no backup or rollback
downsize/optimize signature change from (width, height) to a dimensions string breaks existing call sites, causing TypeError or malformed ImageMagick geometry and silently broken thumbnail generation
In-place from == to convert_with has no failure containment: on ImageMagick error the ignored false return leaves a truncated/corrupted file that gets uploaded with no error surfaced
Client-side upload limit hard-coded to 10MB in utilities.js diverges from the server's max_image_size_kb setting, producing wrong error messages and wasted resample work on sites with smaller limits
Downsize loop mutates bytes before Upload.create_for validations run, so model-layer content checks validate altered data, and a failed URL download (rescue nil) can feed junk into the loop

Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored; convert_with returns false on non-zero exit status and the loop re-runs the identical failing command 5 times, wasting shell invocations before Upload.create_for fails with a generic 'file too large' error with no log of the downsize failure

Fixed 5 iterations of '80%' dimension scaling cannot bridge large size gaps (0.8^5 ≈ 33% linear reduction), so a 9MB image against a 512KB max_image_size_kb exhausts all attempts and the feature fails for the largest uploads, running 5 CPU-bound ImageMagick passes before rejection

Animated-image dispatch in optimized_image.rb keys on the file extension (.gif), but the caller passes a Tempfile path with no .gif extension, so allow_animation is dead code and animated GIFs are silently converted to static first-frame images with no error or log

Downsize reads and writes the same path (tempfile.path, tempfile.path), an unsupported in-place ImageMagick operation; failure mid-write truncates or empties the tempfile and Upload.create_for runs against a corrupted/empty file

Client-side check is hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types while the server still enforces per-type settings commonly far below 10MB, so users pass the client gate and only hit server rejection after the full upload

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate definition of `downsize` in app/models/optimized_image.rb: the new 4-param version silently overrides the existing 5-param one, breaking existing callers with ArgumentError
downsize loop in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-69 writes ImageMagick output to the same path it reads from, which ImageMagick refuses or corrupts

adjudication.rationale: The newly added loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, passing the same file path for both input (`from`) and output (`to`). In `OptimizedImage`, `convert_with` executes an ImageMagick command built from `from` and `to` without any temp-file swap shown in the diff, so this is effectively an in-place convert. In-place writes are commonly unsupported/unsafe for ImageMagick and can fail or corrupt the file, making this a plausible correctness defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Passing "80%" as the dimensions argument to downsize_instructions/downsize_instructions_animated produces malformed geometry/command lines for animated GIFs, causing server-side upload failures
matched_golden_ids: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root cause: using a percentage ("80%") as the resize geometry for the animated GIF path results in invalid/malformed geometry for gifsicle’s resize operation (which expects WxH), so the animated downsizing doesn’t work as intended. The candidate differs on the observed symptom (upload failure vs silent no-op), but the underlying issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded 10 * 1024 limit in utilities.js:182 and :246 decouples client-side gate from max_image_size_kb server setting, making the downsizing feature unreachable for files between the setting and 10MB
Client-side check drops max_attachment_size_kb, hardcoding a 10MB ceiling for all upload types, blocking larger attachments the admin configured

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the client-side file size limit is changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) for all upload types, and the 413 handler similarly hardcodes `10 * 1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. This will cause the browser to reject uploads larger than 10MB even if the admin configured higher `max_*_size_kb` limits (e.g., for attachments), effectively blocking allowed uploads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 413 handler hardcodes 'max 10MB' in the alert regardless of the server's actual limit or nginx client_max_body_size, giving wrong rejection reasons

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the 413 (Payload Too Large) handler now sets `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` (10MB) unconditionally, replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. This will display an incorrect “file too large” limit if the actual server/webserver body limit (or configured site setting) differs, leading to misleading rejection feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No handling for when 5 downsize attempts still leave an image over max_image_size_kb, resulting in a raw 'file too large' rejection

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new loop attempts up to 5 `OptimizedImage.downsize` passes while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but after the loop it unconditionally proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` without checking whether the file is still over the limit or providing a specific error/message for the “downsizing failed to get under max” case. If it remains too large, it will fall back to whatever `Upload.create_for`/validation does (likely a generic too-large failure), which matches the finding as an unhandled edge-case/UX gap introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize failure is silently ignored; in-place from == to downsize corrupts the tempfile when ImageMagick fails or is killed mid-write, uploading corrupted bytes

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e. it performs an in-place conversion where `from == to`. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` shells out to ImageMagick and returns `false` on nonzero exit, but the caller ignores the return value and proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` using whatever bytes are in the tempfile. If ImageMagick fails or is killed during an in-place write, the tempfile contents can be left partially written/corrupt, and that corruption would be uploaded without detection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: def self.downsize is defined twice in the same class body, shadowing the first definition and breaking existing two-argument callers with invalid ImageMagick geometry
Animated GIFs are silently converted to static images when allow_animated_thumbnails is off; allow_animated_avatars is never consulted and original upload animation is destroyed

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, large images are automatically downsized in-place (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`). In `optimized_image.rb`, `optimize` only uses the `_animated` instruction path when `opts[:allow_animation]` is truthy and the file is a GIF; otherwise it uses the non-animated instructions, which would drop animation for GIFs. This new upload-time downsizing therefore can silently destroy GIF animation when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is off, and the code never consults any `allow_animated_avatars` setting (it always uses `allow_animated_thumbnails`) even though the upload `type` could plausibly be avatars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests or assertions for any of the changed behavior, including the convergence loop, in-place file mutation, method redefinition, and client-side limit change

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior (a 5-iteration downsizing loop mutating the tempfile in-place in `UploadsController#create_upload`, refactors `OptimizedImage` APIs including a new `downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts)` signature, and hard-codes a 10MB client-side limit in `utilities.js`), but the shown changes include no accompanying spec/test changes to validate these behaviors. While existing tests might exist elsewhere, the diff itself introduces logic that would typically warrant coverage and adds none here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side size check in utilities.js:182 hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types, silently disabling admin-configured limits like max_attachment_size_kb for non-image uploads
Hardcoded 10MB client-side message desynchronizes from actual server-side enforced limit, showing users '10MB' when server rejects at a different setting value

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes the client-side max size to 10*1024 KB in two places (utilities.js: file size pre-check and 413 handler), replacing use of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. Server-side logic still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (and other `max_*_size_kb` settings likely still exist), so if the configured limit differs from 10MB the UI will display/allow 10MB while the server may reject at the configured value, causing the desynchronization described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 413 handler in utilities.js:246 always claims a 10MB limit even when the server rejected at a type-specific setting, misleading users about attachments

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js` the 413 (entity too large) handler changes `maxSizeKB` from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). That means the user-facing error message will always claim a 10MB limit regardless of the configured per-type/site limits or whatever limit actually triggered the 413, which is misleading behavior introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb:55 hardcodes the API-URL download cap at 10MB via FileHelper.download, discarding SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb for the API path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the API URL download limit in `uploads_controller.rb` from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). This verifiably stops honoring the configured `max_image_size_kb` for the API-URL path (and can also prevent downloads >10MB even if the site setting allows larger), which is a functional behavior change/inconsistency introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsizing loop in uploads_controller.rb:63-70 enforces no invariant that the file ends up under the limit; after 5 failed attempts or when convert_with returns false, the oversized tempfile is passed to Upload.create_for with no size check or user-facing error

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb a new loop attempts to shrink oversized images, but it neither checks the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` nor re-validates `tempfile.size` after the loop; regardless of whether downsizing failed (e.g., convert failure or no size reduction), it proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` with the possibly still-oversized tempfile. Whether this becomes a user-visible bug depends on downstream enforcement inside `Upload.create_for`/model validations, which is not shown in the diff, so the finding is a concrete edge-case/incompleteness concern but not strictly verifiable as a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unscoped refactor of OptimizedImage's resize/downsize/optimize signatures from (width, height) to a free-form dimensions string, weakening type safety for existing callers and deleting dimensions(width, height)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does refactor `OptimizedImage.optimize` to take a single `dimensions` string instead of `(width, height)` and removes the `dimensions(width, height)` helper. `resize`/`downsize` now build a string like `"#{width}x#{height}"`, and there is also a new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` overload added. This is a real, diff-grounded API/scope change that could affect existing callers (and is less structured than separate width/height), but the diff alone doesn’t prove a concrete runtime break elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Ruby method redefinition: downsize is defined twice in optimized_image.rb; the second definition silently shadows the first, so old 5-argument callers pass opts into dimensions and produce garbage geometry strings
matched_golden_ids: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: `downsize` is defined twice, and the second definition overrides/shadows the first. This makes the original signature (separate width/height params) unreachable and breaks existing callers that pass separate arguments, causing them to be misinterpreted as a single dimensions parameter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsizing only fires when FileHelper.is_image?(filename), and filename from URI.parse(url).path may lack an extension for API-downloaded files, so downsizing silently never runs for extension-less API uploads

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing block in `uploads_controller.rb` is gated on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`. For API URL uploads, `filename` is derived from `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`, which can be extension-less (e.g. URLs without a file extension). If `is_image?` is extension-based (not shown in the diff), this would prevent downsizing from running for such images, making the new “auto-reduce” behavior incomplete for that edge case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb:63-68 uses the same tempfile.path as both from and to in OptimizedImage.downsize, corrupting the upload file because ImageMagick truncates the output before fully reading the input

adjudication.rationale: The added loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, passing the same filesystem path as both the source (`from`) and destination (`to`). From the diff, `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately shells out via `convert_with(instructions, to)`, implying an external ImageMagick/convert invocation writing to `to`. Using the same file for input and output is a well-known unsafe pattern for converters and can lead to truncation/corruption if the tool opens the output for writing before fully reading the input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb:64-68 passes '80%' as the dimensions argument, which is not valid for the rewritten optimize pipeline expecting 'WxH' format parsed via split("x")

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedImage.optimize` now takes a `dimensions` string and passes it directly to `*_instructions` methods (`instructions = self.send(..., dimensions, opts)`). There is no evidence in the diff that `dimensions` is parsed via `split("x")` or otherwise requires a `WxH` format. While `uploads_controller.rb` passes "80%", the rewritten pipeline in this diff does not demonstrate that this is invalid or would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb:62-69 downsize loop has no success check or failure path, so still-oversized files proceed to Upload.create_for if 5 iterations of 80% scaling can't reach max_image_size_kb

adjudication.rationale: The added downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` will always fall through to `Upload.create_for(...)` after up to 5 attempts, even if `tempfile.size` remains greater than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. The diff shows no post-loop check or explicit failure path for the “couldn’t downsize enough” case. Whether this becomes an actual bug depends on validations inside `Upload.create_for` (not shown in the diff), but the missing handling is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: utilities.js:182 and :246 hardcodes a 10MB client limit while the server still enforces the configurable SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, producing guaranteed user-facing failures and misleading 413 error messages

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js` the max upload size checks and 413 messaging are changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings[...]` / `max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) for all types. The server side still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (e.g., downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb`) and other server-side limits may still be settings-driven, so client-side validation and error messaging can diverge from actual server enforcement (allowing uploads the server may reject or rejecting uploads that a higher setting would allow).

adjudication_records.issue_text: optimized_image.rb:145-147 defines a duplicate downsize method; the first definition is dead code and any 4-arg call gets silently reinterpreted by the second definition

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb` the diff leaves an existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` below it. In Ruby, the later definition overwrites the earlier one, making the first dead code. This also risks breaking any existing 4-arg positional calls (e.g., `downsize(from,to,w,h)`), which would now be interpreted as `dimensions=w` and `opts=h` (non-Hash), likely causing errors when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed in `optimize`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uploads_controller.rb:68 performs blocking 5x full-image convert forks on the request path, risking web worker saturation for concurrent large uploads

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a synchronous downsizing loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can run up to 5 iterations (`attempt = 5` / `while attempt > 0 ... OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`). `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately calls `convert_with`, which shells out via backticks to run the image conversion command, i.e., a blocking external process on the request thread. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/saturation risk for concurrent large uploads, but it’s not a correctness/security defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side size gate hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring admin-configured max_image_size_kb and per-type settings, so files between the configured limit and 10MB pass client validation
matched_golden_ids: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: the client enforces a hardcoded 10MB (10*1024 KB) limit instead of using the server/admin-configured per-type SiteSetting (max_<type>_size_kb), leading to client/server (and per-type) divergence where oversized files may pass client validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Files between configured limit and 10MB get silently downsized server-side or fail at Upload.create_for with an error contradicting the pre-upload message

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes the client-side max upload size to 10MB (`maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`) and also reports 10MB on HTTP 413, instead of using `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `max_image_size_kb`. Server-side, `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` is still used (and new logic attempts to downsize images until under that configured limit). This creates a real mismatch: files larger than the configured limit but under 10MB will pass the pre-upload check and may then be downsized silently or rejected later due to the smaller server-side limit, contradicting what the client communicated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 413 error path reports a fixed 10MB limit instead of the actual max_image_size_kb enforced by the server, misleading users to retry under a limit that will fail again

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the 413 (entity too large) alert was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hard-coded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This can misreport the actual configured limit (`max_image_size_kb`) and mislead users about what size will succeed, especially since server-side logic in `uploads_controller.rb` still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` for downsizing/limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsizing loop mutates the user's uploaded file in place before validation, changing contract from rejecting oversized images to silently altering them without consent or notice

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that, when the upload is an image and exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, overwriting the same tempfile in place before `Upload.create_for(...)` runs. There is no user-facing notice in this controller path that the image was modified; the intent is stated in the comment (“allow users to upload large images that will be automatically reduced”). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/contract change (silent alteration) but appears intentional rather than an outright correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsizing potentially strips animation via allow_animation: allow_animated_thumbnails, a thumbnail-specific setting, and applies to every image above the limit even if it would otherwise be rejected

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` runs for any oversize image (`FileHelper.is_image?`) and calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, GIFs only use the `*_instructions_animated` path when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true; otherwise they use the non-animated instructions, which can change/strip animation for large GIF uploads. This is a behavior/data-loss risk introduced by the diff, and it ties animation preservation to a setting named for thumbnails rather than uploads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: downsize overload collapses width/height into a free-form dimensions string; passing '80%' uses ImageMagick percentage geometry which upscales and does not respect the shrink-only size-bounds contract existing callers rely on

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` to take a preformatted `dimensions` string, and `uploads_controller.rb` now calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`. However, the finding’s core claim that using the ImageMagick geometry string `"80%"` “upscales” and violates an existing shrink-only bounds contract is not verifiable from the diff: `80%` is a downscale factor, and the diff does not show any prior or current “shrink-only size-bounds contract” (e.g., use of `>` geometry) that callers rely on. The assertion about upscaling/contract breach is therefore unsupported by what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side download size limit replaced with hardcoded 10.megabytes, discarding SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, allowing bypass of admin-configured bandwidth/disk controls

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the API URL download size limit changes from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`, so the admin-configured `max_image_size_kb` no longer constrains server-side downloads (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). This can allow downloading larger files than intended when the setting is lower, bypassing configured limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DoS amplification via repeated synchronous shell-outs: OptimizedImage.downsize runs up to 5 times per upload on attacker-supplied bytes with no timeout or shrink check, enabling decompression-bomb CPU exhaustion

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new synchronous downsizing loop in `UploadsController#create_upload`: up to 5 iterations of `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` on attacker-controlled uploads (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`). `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately calls `convert_with`, which shell-outs via backticks (no timeout/limits shown in the diff). This change can multiply the CPU/work per request (up to 5 expensive image conversions) for oversized or “hard to downsize” images, creating a plausible DoS amplification vector compared to the prior single-pass behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Content-type/size validation gate trusts client-controlled filename extension (FileHelper.is_image?) instead of content-sniffing magic bytes, allowing non-image payloads to pass and compound DoS

adjudication.rationale: The new server-side downsizing block in `uploads_controller.rb` is gated by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, which is derived from a client/URL-provided filename (`filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)` or upload filename). This suggests an extension-based check (it only receives `filename`), not content sniffing. As a result, a non-image payload named `*.jpg`/`*.png` can trigger up to 5 ImageMagick/convert operations via `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` (which shells out), and failures aren’t checked, creating a tangible security/resource-exhaustion risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side size ceiling hardcoded to 10 * 1024 KB, removing SiteSetting['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] enforcement from UX and causing misleading user-facing errors

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the client-side size limit is changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` in both the pre-upload check and the 413 handler. This removes per-site/per-type setting enforcement on the client and can produce incorrect validation and misleading “file too large” messages when the server-side `SiteSetting.*_size_kb` differs from 10MB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:142-148 — `def self.downsize` is defined twice in the same module; the second definition silently overrides the first, so callers using the 4-arg form pass `max_width` as the `dimensions` string and drop `max_height`, producing incorrectly-sized thumbnails or failed convert calls

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/optimized_image.rb the diff leaves an existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` below it. In Ruby, the latter definition overwrites the former, so any existing callers using the 4-arg (width,height) form will now either raise an ArgumentError (too many args) or mis-bind `max_height` into `opts` (non-Hash), leading to incorrect behavior or runtime errors when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed in `optimize`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-70 — the downsize loop mutates `tempfile` in place but `Upload.create_for` reads `tempfile.size` after the loop; if ImageMagick fails (exitstatus swallowed by `convert_with`), the oversized file is passed to `Upload.create_for` causing errors

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` in-place, but it never checks whether the downsize succeeded. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` on nonzero exit status, yet `optimize`/`downsize` ignore that return value, so ImageMagick failures are effectively silent. If downsizing fails (or doesn’t reduce below `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` within 5 attempts), the loop ends and `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` is still called with an oversized file, likely causing upload errors rather than a controlled rejection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-70 — the filename's original extension / extension-vs-content is never re-validated after downsizing

adjudication.rationale: The added downsizing loop mutates `tempfile` in-place before `Upload.create_for(...)`, but the diff does not show what validation `Upload.create_for` performs on filename/extension vs content (it may already validate content type/magic). The finding asserts that extension/content is “never re-validated after downsizing,” which cannot be confirmed from the shown changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-70 — the loop uses "80%" geometry, which under the new string-dimensions signature is a percentage scale rather than a pixel bound, so 5 passes yield at most ~67% linear reduction, failing silently for large images with no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` while the file is still larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, but it stops after 5 attempts and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` without any explicit handling if the image is still oversized. Using a percentage geometry like "80%" is a scale factor (not a pixel bound), so it may or may not reduce filesize enough within 5 passes, and the diff shows no user-facing message when the downsizing attempts are exhausted. However, the finding’s specific claim about the signature change *causing* this behavior and its reduction math aren’t strictly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedImage.downsize overwrites the source tempfile in place with a lossy resample, permanently destroying the user's original upload even if the upload ultimately fails validation, with no backup or rollback

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, i.e. it writes the downsized output back to the same tempfile path, so the originally received bytes are no longer available on the server side (and this happens before `Upload.create_for` validation succeeds). However, the diff comment explicitly intends to “automatically reduce” large images, so overwriting the input looks like an implementation/design choice rather than a clearly unintended correctness defect; the review point is a valid concern about mutating the only copy with no fallback if later steps fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: downsize/optimize signature change from (width, height) to a dimensions string breaks existing call sites, causing TypeError or malformed ImageMagick geometry and silently broken thumbnail generation

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, `downsize` is defined twice: first as `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, then immediately redefined as `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the latter overwrites the former, so any existing call sites still passing `(from, to, width, height, opts)` will now raise an `ArgumentError` (wrong number of arguments) at runtime. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable breaking change and can break thumbnail/image processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place from == to convert_with has no failure containment: on ImageMagick error the ignored false return leaves a truncated/corrupted file that gets uploaded with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: The new upload-path resizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` (from == to), and `OptimizedImage.convert_with` explicitly returns `false` on ImageMagick failure, but the controller ignores that return and proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)`. The diff therefore exposes a real failure-handling bug: a failed in-place conversion can still lead to uploading whatever is left in `tempfile` (potentially corrupted/truncated or still oversize) with no surfaced error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side upload limit hard-coded to 10MB in utilities.js diverges from the server's max_image_size_kb setting, producing wrong error messages and wasted resample work on sites with smaller limits

adjudication.rationale: In utilities.js the max upload size check is changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hard-coded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in both the pre-upload size check and the 413 error handler. This demonstrably diverges from server-side configurable limits (e.g., `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` still exists and is used in uploads_controller.rb), so on sites with smaller limits the client can (a) allow an upload that the server may reject and (b) show an incorrect `max_size_kb` value in the error message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize loop mutates bytes before Upload.create_for validations run, so model-layer content checks validate altered data, and a failed URL download (rescue nil) can feed junk into the loop

adjudication.rationale: The added downsize loop in `uploads_controller.rb` is guarded (`if tempfile && tempfile.size > 0 ...`) so a failed URL download (`tempfile = ... rescue nil`) will not enter the loop. Also, mutating the tempfile before `Upload.create_for` means validations see the final (downsized) bytes, which is the intended behavior for “automatically reduced to allowed size”; the diff doesn’t show any requirement that validations must run on the original bytes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored; convert_with returns false on non-zero exit status and the loop re-runs the identical failing command 5 times, wasting shell invocations before Upload.create_for fails with a generic 'file too large' error with no log of the downsize failure

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` and ignores its return value. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` on non-zero exit status (and otherwise returns `nil`), so a failing downsize won’t be detected. Because the loop condition is based on `tempfile.size` and there’s no break/log on failure, the same failing conversion can be invoked up to 5 times with no diagnostic output (`&> /dev/null`). This is a diff-grounded robustness/performance/observability issue more than a strictly new functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fixed 5 iterations of '80%' dimension scaling cannot bridge large size gaps (0.8^5 ≈ 33% linear reduction), so a 9MB image against a 512KB max_image_size_kb exhausts all attempts and the feature fails for the largest uploads, running 5 CPU-bound ImageMagick passes before rejection

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new downsizing loop is hardcoded to at most 5 iterations and always applies `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)` while the condition is `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. From the diff alone, there’s no guarantee this fixed number of passes and fixed scale factor will bring an arbitrarily large image under the configured byte limit, so some oversized images may still remain above the limit after 5 CPU-intensive ImageMagick runs and then proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` still too large (likely to be rejected by downstream validations). The specific numeric example (9MB -> 512KB) isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the general edge-case/inefficiency is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated-image dispatch in optimized_image.rb keys on the file extension (.gif), but the caller passes a Tempfile path with no .gif extension, so allow_animation is dead code and animated GIFs are silently converted to static first-frame images with no error or log

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, animated dispatch is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is truthy **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The new upload downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`; `tempfile.path` typically has no `.gif` extension, so the regex won’t match and the `_animated` instruction path will never be used even for animated GIF uploads. This makes the `allow_animation` option effectively inert for this caller and can lead to animated GIFs being processed with the non-animated pipeline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize reads and writes the same path (tempfile.path, tempfile.path), an unsupported in-place ImageMagick operation; failure mid-write truncates or empties the tempfile and Upload.create_for runs against a corrupted/empty file

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, passing the same pathname for both input and output. In `optimized_image.rb`, `downsize` ultimately runs an external ImageMagick command via `convert_with(instructions, to)` without any guard against `from == to` and without checking the return value in the controller. If the underlying convert operation does not safely support in-place writes (or fails mid-write), this can leave `tempfile` corrupted/empty, and the code still proceeds to `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` using whatever is left on disk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side check is hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types while the server still enforces per-type settings commonly far below 10MB, so users pass the client gate and only hit server rejection after the full upload

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js` the client-side size gate is changed from per-type settings (`Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`) to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB (10MB) for all uploads and for 413 errors. On the server side, the diff still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` as the target limit for images (the downsize loop), implying the effective allowed size can be lower than 10MB. That creates a mismatch where the client may accept files up to 10MB but the server may still reject (or need to downsize) based on `max_image_size_kb`/per-type limits, meaning users can pass the client check and only fail after uploading.
